chunks: A group of scholars informed us from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, who said: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Muktabib told me: I was in the City of Peace (Baghdad) in the year in which the Shaykh Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samuri (may his soul be sanctified) passed away. I visited him a few days before his death, and he brought out a Tawqi' (letter) to the people, the text of which was: In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

O Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samuri, may Allah increase the reward of your brothers for you, for you shall die within six days. Tie up your affairs and do not appoint anyone to succeed you after your death, for the Complete Occultation has occurred, and there shall be no Appearance except by permission of Allah, exalted is His mention, and that will be after a long period, hardening of the hearts, and the earth being filled with injustice. And my Shia will come, one who claims to have seen me. Behold, whoever claims to have seen me before the emergence of al-Sufyani and the Call is a liar and a fabricator. And there is no power and no strength except with Allah, the High, the Great.

He said: We transcribed this Tawqi' and left him. When it was the sixth day, we returned to him as he was breathing his last. He was asked: Who is your successor after you? He said: To Allah belongs the Order, and He is its Doer, and He has decreed. This was the last word we heard from him, may Allah be pleased with him and pleased him.

key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him
key_terms.وَالصَّيْحَةُ: And the Call (a major eschatological sign)

ai.seo_question: What happened during the final days of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samuri regarding the Complete Occultation?
ai.summary: This hadith marks the pivotal transition from the Minor to the Major Occultation, as Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Samuri, the final deputy, received a divine directive not to appoint a successor, thereby ending the era of exclusive claimants. The text emphasizes the prolonged nature of the Major Occultation, characterized by 'hardness of hearts' and global injustice, while providing a critical criterion for distinguishing true from false claimants: any assertion of direct sighting before the emergence of the Sufyani and the Call (al-Sayhah) is deemed false. This narrative solidifies the Shia theological stance on the continuity of divine guidance despite the Imam's physical absence.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 365 - It is narrated from a group of scholars from Abu Ja’far Muhammad Ibn Ali Ibn Husain Ibn Babawayh that Abu Muhammad Hasan Ibn Ahmad Mukattib said: I was in Baghdad in the year in which Shaykh Abul Hasan Ali Ibn Muhammad Saymoori passed away. I went to him a few days before his demise. He brought a holy letter to the people that read as follows: “In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

O Ali Ibn Muhammad Saymoori, may Allah enhance the reward of your brothers for you, as you shall die within six days. Tie up your affairs together and do not appoint any successor to carry out your duties after your final transfer. The full occultation has begun and there shall be no appearance, but after permission of Allah, high His name is, and that shall be after a long time, hardening of the hearts and the earth being replete with inequity. Individuals from my Shia will claim to have seen me. Behold, whoever claims seeing me before the rise of Sufyani and the call, is a liar and a slanderer. And there is no power except by Allah, the High, the Great.”

We transcribed copies of the holy letter and left him. When it was the sixth day, we returned to him as he was breathing his last. He was asked, “Who is your successor after you?” He said: “To Allah belongs the Order and He is its Sustainer.” He died. These were the last words heard from him. May Allah be pleased with him and may He please him.
